items.title: Theorem 1: random-channel violation of von Neumann minimum-output-entropy additivity
items.statement_scope: Whole Theorem 1 (label mainthm): there exist sufficiently large D and, depending on D, sufficiently large N such that with non-zero probability over independent Haar-random N-by-N unitaries U_i (i=1,...,D) and random weights P_i=l_i^2/L^2, L^2=sum_i l_i^2, with l_i independently drawn from P(l_i) proportional to l_i^(2N-1) exp(-ND l_i^2), the channel E defined at combined.tex:140-143 and its complex-conjugate channel Ebar defined at combined.tex:145-147 satisfy the strict inequality H^min(E⊗Ebar) < H^min(E)+H^min(Ebar)=2H^min(E). Here H^min(F)=min over pure |ψ> of the von Neumann output entropy H(F(|ψ><ψ|)), in the p=1/von Neumann setting, not a Renyi-p surrogate. The theorem asserts non-zero probability, not probability one; N depends on D; the analysis uses 1<<D<<N.

standard_prerequisites: von Neumann entropy H(ρ)=-Tr(ρ ln ρ), Holevo chi, and minimum output entropy H^min(E)=min over pure |ψ> of H(E(|ψ><ψ|)) (combined.tex:73-77,107-110).
Quantum channel as a linear completely positive trace-preserving map, and the conjugate-channel identity H^min(E)=H^min(E^C) cited to King-Matsumoto-Nathanson-Ruskai (combined.tex:54-59,359-369).
Haar measure on U(N), and random weights l_i independent with P(l_i) proportional to l_i^(2N-1)exp(-ND l_i^2), L^2=sum_i l_i^2, P_i=l_i^2/L^2 (combined.tex:323-353).
Computer-science big-O convention as explicitly fixed by the author (combined.tex:371-379).
Operator monotonicity of the logarithm (combined.tex:462-474, citing Bhatia).
Page and Lloyd-Pagels random bipartite eigenvalue distribution (combined.tex:557-565, citing Page and Lloyd-Pagels).

items.difficulty_reason: H3 under author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: the counted statement at combined.tex:159-172 is the paper's main research-bearing counterexample, not a routine corollary. The author constructs E and Ebar from Haar-random unitaries and random weights (combined.tex:133-156,323-353); obtains the entangled-input upper bound through operator-monotonicity/log inequalities and Cauchy-Schwarz (combined.tex:402-519); and proves the product-input lower bound through random bipartite eigenvalue estimates, conditioning, and constrained maximization arguments (combined.tex:521-627,715-767,773-909,911-1065).

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: The strict random-channel inequality is borne by the maximally entangled input bound and Cauchy-Schwarz analysis at 402-519 together with the random bipartite eigenvalue, conditioning, and constrained-maximization argument through 1065; these are substantive research arguments, not routine preliminary facts.

semantic_comparisons.comparison: Not the same result. The neighbour is a combinatorial lemma: for each dimension d>=2 there exist s(d)=d generalized Bell states when d is odd and s(d)=3d/2 when d is even, lying in the antisymmetric-subspace orthogonal complement, with a proof by symmetric matrices and block shifts. The counted Hastings theorem is an existential probabilistic statement over sufficiently large D and N(D): random Haar unitaries and random supplemental weights produce a channel E whose complex conjugate Ebar strictly violates additivity of p=1/von Neumann minimum output entropy, H^min(E⊗Ebar)<2H^min(E). Hypotheses, quantifiers, mathematical objects, and conclusions differ. The overlap is only the broad topic of additivity counterexamples and Bell states. No same statement, proof, translation, or version.
